Keywords: astro, static, content site, mpa, islands, fastest, seo, blog, brochure
When To Choose: Default for content-led sites with little client interactivity. Best Lighthouse per unit of effort
Scaffold Commands: npm create astro@latest -- --template minimal; npx astro add tailwind; npx astro add sitemap
Prerender Approach: Static HTML at build time by default; zero JS unless an island is declared
Routing: File-based routes in src/pages; anchors within a page
Deploy: vercel/netlify/cloudflare static output; no server needed
Tradeoffs: Islands architecture means less shared client state; GSAP work must live inside a client-directive island
Gotchas: client:visible is the right directive for scroll animation islands; client:load pulls the framework into the critical path

Keywords: vite, react, spa, single page, gsap, three, r3f, fast dev, custom
When To Choose: Single-page experiential site with heavy motion or WebGL where the whole page is one React tree
Scaffold Commands: npm create vite@latest -- --template react-ts; npm i -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite; npm i gsap lenis; npm i vite-plugin-prerender-or-equivalent
Key Dependencies: react, react-dom, gsap, lenis, tailwindcss; optional three, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei
Prerender Approach: Client-rendered by default — this is the trap. Add a prerender step (vite-prerender-plugin, vite-plugin-ssr, or a Puppeteer post-build) so the HTML ships with real content
Routing: Anchor-based sections on one route; react-router only when a second real route exists
Deploy: vercel/netlify static output with a SPA rewrite
Tradeoffs: Fastest to build and the most freedom for motion; worst default SEO and unfurl behaviour until prerendering is added
Gotchas: An empty <div id=root> in the built HTML means crawlers, link previews and no-JS visitors see nothing. Verify with curl on the production build, not in dev

Keywords: next, nextjs, app router, ssg, react server components, seo, multi page
When To Choose: Multiple real routes plus React, or when a CMS or a form route will be added later
Key Dependencies: next, react, tailwindcss; gsap and lenis in client components only
Prerender Approach: Static generation per route by default in the App Router; metadata API for titles, OG and canonical
Routing: File-based app router; generateStaticParams for content collections
Deploy: vercel first-class; static export with output: export when no server features are used
Tradeoffs: More framework than a one-page site needs; the payoff is metadata, routing and a growth path
Gotchas: GSAP and Lenis must live in components marked 'use client' and be registered inside useEffect or useGSAP; ScrollTrigger must be refreshed after route transitions

Keywords: html, vanilla, no framework, plain, hand coded, minimal js
When To Choose: Single page with fewer than about eight sections and no component reuse pressure
Scaffold Commands: mkdir site; npm i -D vite tailwindcss @tailwindcss/cli; create index.html
Key Dependencies: vite for the dev server and build, tailwindcss or plain CSS custom properties, gsap
Prerender Approach: Nothing to prerender — the HTML is the source
Tradeoffs: Lowest possible weight and no framework churn; content duplication once sections repeat
Gotchas: Without a component layer, a token change means editing many places. Introduce Astro before hand-maintaining a third near-identical block

Keywords: r3f, three, 3d, webgl, react three fiber, drei, model
When To Choose: Added on top of recipe 2 or 3 when a WebGL centrepiece is justified
Scaffold Commands: npm i three @react-three/fiber @react-three/drei; npm i -D @types/three; npx gltfjsx model.glb --transform
Key Dependencies: three, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei; gltfjsx and gltf-transform as dev tools
Prerender Approach: The canvas never prerenders — the poster image does
Routing: Canvas mounted inside one section, dynamically imported
Tradeoffs: One justified centrepiece is the difference between premium and bloated
Gotchas: gltfjsx --transform runs Draco plus texture resizing and typically cuts the GLB by 70-90 percent. Always run it before committing the asset

Keywords: content, cms, mdx, typed content, copy management, editing, handoff
When To Choose: Any site whose copy the client will want to change without touching components
Scaffold Commands: mkdir -p src/content; create content.ts exporting typed objects, or npx astro add mdx
Key Dependencies: typescript; optional zod for content validation; optional MDX
Prerender Approach: Content is imported at build time; no runtime fetch
Tradeoffs: A typed content module makes copy reviewable in one diff and prevents strings drifting into components
Gotchas: Validate the content object with zod at build time so a missing phone number fails the build instead of rendering 'undefined' in production
